subject: MAP: Stress-grid benchmarking, TTFT targets, and close cadence
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@orionhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: perf targets & timeline

Hi Neha / team,

Thanks for making time today. As discussed on the call, Orion wants a short MAP that documents: the perf evaluation plan, acceptance criteria for the POC, and a close timeline that aligns procurement and engineering. Our primary production goals are: p95 latency <= 350ms for single-turn streaming responses, sustained throughput at 200 concurrent sessions with typical 40-token responses, and TTFT <= 120ms for the first token on our west-coast region.

Can you share a stress-grid plan (concurrency x request size), the exact metrics you will collect, and which model variants you'll include from Redwood's catalog? I'm attaching the baseline MAP template we use (orion_map_v1.xlsx).

Jamie
Director, Product
Orion Health

Attachment: orion_map_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet - MAP template)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: perf targets & timeline

Thanks Jamie — appreciate the clear targets. High level plan below; I'll turn this into the MAP spreadsheet and share by end of day.

Planned evaluation (short summary):
- Stress-grid: concurrency [1, 10, 50, 100, 200, 400] x request sizes [20t, 40t, 100t]. Run 10min ramps at each point to stabilize error/latency.
- Metrics captured: TTFT, per-token latency breakdown (generation vs network), p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, memory footprint, and error rates.
- Model variants to include from Redwood catalog (initial):
  * Redwood-7B-OPT (FP16 baseline) — higher quality/low latency sweet spot for short responses
  * Llama2-13B-Quant (int8) — quality trade for denser context when throughput matters
  * Redwood-13B-AVA (optimized kernels) — higher quality, expect +20% cost but better coherence 
  * Small distilled variant (gpt-3.5-like proxy) — fallback for bursty traffic
- Workload shape: streaming enabled (we'll measure TTFT separately), and batched closed-loop for synthetic bulk throughput tests.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- POC passes at least 2 of 3 checkpoints: TTFT target, p95 latency target, and sustained 200 concurrent sessions with error rate < 1%.
- Quality: top-line semantic similarity metric (ROUGE/BLEU not ideal) — we'll use human-annotated sample set plus automatic embedding-similarity thresholds.

Deliverables & dates (draft):
- 2027-06-19: MAP spreadsheet v1 + test harness repo link
- 2027-06-21: Run stress-grid tests and share raw results
- 2027-06-22: Consolidated results + recommended variant for production
- 2027-06-25: Mutual sign-off (engineering + procurement) / procurement T&Cs

I'll include the test harness (small k6 + python runner) so Orion can reproduce. Any changes to targets, flag them and we'll update the MAP.

-Neha
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: stress_grid_results_june18.pdf (PDF - plan summary)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: perf targets & timeline

Quick technical clarifications — please add to the MAP before we share: 

1) Concurrency semantics: are we measuring concurrent user sessions (each streaming) or concurrent inference pipelines (batched requests)? We should define both.
2) Token distribution: send us a small sample of 200 real requests (or generate via Canonical suite) — critical for kernel selection and KV cache sizing.
3) Network expectations: we'll run tests from our west-coast region (us-west-2). If Orion will test from a private VPC, we need to coordinate NAT/GW endpoints to measure pure runtime TTFT vs customer network latency.
4) Logging/tracing: we will include per-request trace IDs and a CSV with per-token timing. Need to confirm retention window for results.

Also proposing one extra model variant: Redwood-Quant-7B (int8) — often hits a much lower cost per token with acceptable quality for short-turn dialogs. If Orion has high relevance/hallucination sensitivity, call out which sample scenarios to gate on.

I'll add these to the MAP tab and drop a link to the harness in the next update.

-Karthik
Sr. Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@orionhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-23T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: MAP v1 + stress-grid results summary and next steps

Jamie / team — attached is MAP v1 and the condensed stress-grid run we executed on 6/21-6/22. The raw CSVs are in the Drive link; below is the executive summary and our recommended variant for production.

Executive summary (key numbers):
- Test harness: k6 + python runner (streaming client). All runs from us-west-2.
- Workload shape used: 200 sample requests (provided by Orion) with token distribution: median 38, 75th 74, 95th 180.

Results by variant (representative metrics):
- Redwood-7B-OPT (FP16): TTFT median 95ms, p95 latency 310ms at 200 concurrent sessions, sustained throughput 1,900 req/min, error rate 0.6%, GPU util 72%. Quality: human panel pass rate 85% (n=60).
- Redwood-Quant-7B (int8): TTFT median 110ms, p95 370ms at 200 concurrent, sustained throughput 2,300 req/min, error 0.9%, GPU util 64%. Quality: human panel pass 78% (n=60). Notable: lower cost (~22% savings) but some degradation on long-coherence prompts.
- Llama2-13B-Quant: TTFT median 145ms, p95 420ms at 200 concurrent, sustained throughput 1,400 req/min, error 1.2%, GPU util 89%. Quality: human panel pass 88% (n=60) on deep-context tests but higher latency/cost.
- Redwood-13B-AVA: TTFT median 105ms, p95 340ms at 200 concurrent, sustained throughput 1,650 req/min, error 0.7%, GPU util 78%. Quality: human panel pass 92% (n=60). Cost premium ~18%.

Recommendation:
- For Orion's stated goals (TTFT <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, 200 concurrent): Redwood-7B-OPT meets TTFT and p95 with acceptable quality at lower cost; Redwood-13B-AVA is a higher-quality option if Orion prefers fewer quality regressions and is willing to accept the cost premium. Quant variants can be used as a cost-lever for non-critical paths.

Next steps / MAP updates:
- 2027-06-24: Deliver full MAP v1 with SOC2 and data retention one-pager (attached).
- 2027-06-25: Procurement and technical sign-off call (confirming SKU and start date).
- Post-sign: Redwood will provide a 2-week production ramp runbook and traffic-split guidance.

Attachments: soc2_evidence_redwood_v3.pdf; stress_grid_results_june18.pdf

-Neha
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
